title: The RUNX1 Research Program 10th Annual Scientific Conference and Patient Meeting
text:
The RUNX1 Research Program 10th Annual Scientific Conference and Patient Meeting fosters
collaboration and provides opportunities for knowledge and data sharing among researchers,
students, clinicians, and patients and their families for a rare disease called RUNX1 familial
platelet disorder with predisposition to hematologic malignancies (RUNX1-FPD - OMIM #
601399FPDMM).

title: Core B: Mass Spectrometry, proteomics, metabolmics and lipidomics
text:
Core B: Narrative 
The mass spectrometry core will provide proteomics/phosphoproteomics, metabolomics and lipidomics services 
for the three major projects from cancer cells, tumor tissue and biological fluids using tandem mass spectrometry 
(LC-MS/MS). These services will support the discovery of novel pathways and drug targets for Hamartoma 
syndromes and related cancers stemming from defects in the tuberous sclerosis complex (TCS1-TSC2) genes.

title: Biomimetic Triphasic Interference Screws for Bone-Ligament/Tendon Regeneration: A Synergistic Approach Combining Design, Manufacturing, and Biological Validation
text:
This research project aims to develop novel triphasic interference screws with biomimetic bone-ligament/tendon tissue
structures using advanced 3D printing techniques to improve musculoskeletal joint repair outcomes. The interference screws
will incorporate zone-specific biochemical modifications to promote simultaneous bone and tendon/ligament regeneration,
addressing the high failure rates in current anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstructions. Through computational
modeling and experimental validation, this project will establish a new paradigm in orthopedic implant design while
providing hands-on research training for undergraduate and high school students in biomedical engineering.

title: CRISPR-based in vivo attenuation of HSV to improve immune control of genital herpes infection
text:
Genital herpes is a lifelong infection that can cause severe disease in newborns and immunocompromised
individuals. The infection involves reoccurring shedding of infectious viral particles in the presence and absence
of clinical manifestations. This project will test the feasibility of therapeutic targeting of a newly identified HSV
immune evasion factor to prevent or reduce genital herpes lesion formation and viral shedding.

title: Intelligent wearable system for preventing medication errors in anesthesiology
text:
Medication errors or adverse events are a major public health problem causing thousands of deaths annually.
This proposal aims to build wearable cameras with real-time computer vision algorithms to identify medications
when initially selected by an anesthesiology provider during drug preparation or before injection to potentially
prevent accidentally giving the wrong drug. Drug dose will also be determined and recorded in an electronic
health record, potentially increasing record accuracy and decreasing manual tasks for anesthesiologists so
they can focus on direct patient care.

title: Identifying drivers of genital inflammation and HIV acquisition in women living in sub-Saharan Africa
text: Of the 1.2 million new infections each year, most occur in young women of reproductive age; the female genital tract (FGT) therefore plays a pivotal role in the acquisition of HIV infection in women. In this project, we will utilize innovative multi-omic characterization of vaginal microbiota and host measures of genital inflammation using samples from a unique clinical cohort of women living in an area of high HIV incidence and prevalence to identify novel biological mechanisms and interventional targets. This research has the potential to inform strategies to decrease new HIV infections in women in the US, by identifying microbial and host pathways that can be targeted to reduce genital inflammation and HIV susceptibility.

title: Role of N-terminal acetylation in alpha synuclein stability, function, and therapeutic targeting in synucleinopathies
text:
α-Synuclein protein levels closely correlate with the risk of several neurodegenerative diseases, including
Parkinson’s Disease and dementias related to Alzheimer’s Disease, termed ADRDs. We recently found, using
unbiased genome-wide screening approaches, that loss of α-synuclein N-terminal acetylation results in a stark
reduction in endogenous protein levels in both model cell lines and neurons. Based on these results, we will
investigate the role of this modification in α-synuclein biology and develop the first small molecule inhibitors of
the NatB enzyme complex responsible for N-terminal acetylation of α-synuclein that we will evaluate for their
therapeutic potential in Parkinson’s Disease and ADRDs.

title: Modeling the effects of the gut microbiota of undernourished mothers with environmental enteric dysfunction on vascular remodeling at the fetal-placental interface
text:
Undernutrition remains a pressing global health problem and the associated poor long-term outcomes are
transmitted from mother to child, perpetuating the cycle of poverty. Environmental enteric dysfunction (EED) is
a small intestinal inflammatory enteropathy that has been postulated to mediate intergenerational pathogenesis
of undernutrition in utero; yet, how maternal EED transmission affects fetal development is not understood.
The goal of this proposal is to investigate the hypothesis that the small intestinal microbiota from EED affected
mothers contributes to delayed fetal development via aberrant placental vascular remodeling by integrating
gnotobiotic mouse models and multi-omic technologies to identify mechanism of intergenerational EED
transmission and ultimately develop therapies targeted towards maternal and child undernutrition.

title: Postdoctoral Training in Drug Abuse Research: Behavior & Neurobiology
text:
Now in its 14th year at the University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio, this Training Program
addresses the growing need for well-trained early-career scientists in substance use disorder (SUD) research
by providing comprehensive research and career development opportunities to promising predoctoral and
postdoctoral trainees. Program Leadership (Co-Directors and a Program Coordinator) continues to improve the
Program with guidance from Internal and External Advisory Committees. All positions have remained filled, and
past trainees have been highly productive, securing successful research or research-related careers in
academia, the private sector, and government.

title: Personalized Spatial Regulatory Networks to Decode Breast Cancer Microenvironments
text:
Triple-negative breast cancer is a highly aggressive disease driven by complex interactions between genetic,
epigenetic, and spatial factors within the tumor microenvironment. This study will develop a novel methodology
integrating spatial ATAC-seq, spatial in situ transcriptomics, and single-nucleus Epi Multiome sequencing from
core-needle biopsies to map patient-specific gene regulatory networks with high resolution. By combining these
technologies, we aim to uncover mechanisms of intra-tumor heterogeneity, epigenetic plasticity, and immune
evasion, providing new insights for precision oncology and targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: Genetic and Cellular Mechanisms of Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
text:
Epilepsy is a serious chronic neurologic condition that affects over 50 million people worldwide, and the
most common form of focal epilepsy, temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), is frequently resistant to medical treatment
resulting in significant neurologic and psychiatric morbidity. Recent research has shown that genetic mutations
that arise after conception (somatic variants) may disrupt normal cellular function in the brain and cause
neuropsychiatric disease. This proposal will examine the hypothesis that somatic mutations cause TLE and it
will aim to identify the cell-types and gene expression changes that contribute to the development of this
disease.

title: Applications of artificial intelligence to the diagnostic evaluation of infectious keratitis
text:
This K23 application aims to develop and validate artificial intelligence tools to aid in determining the
microbiologic etiology of infectious keratitis, which is a major cause of blindness worldwide. We intend to
develop two artificial intelligence systems, one to determine the cause of infectious keratitis from clinical
photographs and the other to read microbiologic smears in an automated fashion. These systems will allow
more rapid initiation of directed antimicrobial therapy, particularly in medically underserved areas, and improve
visual outcomes in infectious keratitis.

title: Chemical Approaches for Exploring Protein Prenylation in Living Cells
text:
This project seeks to develop methods that can be used to study prenylated proteins. This class of
proteins is involved in controlling many key events within cells. These new methods should facilitate
the discovery of new protein targets that could be used to develop new therapeutic agents for the
treatment of a wide range of diseases ranging from Alzheimer’s disease to cancer.

title: VIP Signaling Mechanisms in Thalamocortical Circuit Plasticity and Learning
text:
Plasticity in the cerebral cortex supports learning, memory, and recovery from neurological injury. However, the
cellular and circuit-level mechanisms that enable this adaptive remodeling remain incompletely understood. This
project investigates how the neuropeptide vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) is released during sensory learning
and modulates cortical circuit dynamics to drive long-term synaptic plasticity. By elucidating fundamental
principles of neuropeptide signaling, this research aims to identify novel therapeutic targets to enhance functional
recovery in neurological conditions such as stroke, epilepsy, and neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: MWCCS– SF Bay Area MACS/WIHS Combined Cohort Study
text:
The San Francisco Bay Area Clinical Research Site (SF CRS) of the MACS-WIHS Combined Cohort Study
(MWCCS) proposes four operational and four scientific aims to expand MWCCS’ impact through mentorship of
early-stage investigators in research and leadership, innovative retention strategies for an aging cohort of men
and women with and without HIV, and deep phenotyping integrated with omics. Scientific aims will examine the
effects of HIV and biomarker-based substance use/co-use on organ function; the role of chronological,
epigenetic, and ovarian aging in HIV pathogenesis and comorbidities; and the acceptability and clinical utility of
pharmacogenomic testing to guide statin therapy in people with HIV. Through collaborative leadership and
translational research, SF CRS aims to generate actionable insights to reduce the burden of chronic diseases in
populations aging with HIV.

title: Causal Dynamics of Human Amygdala-Prefrontal Circuits during Fear Extinction Learning
text:
Exposure-based therapies are the primary behavioral treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), but their
effects are often short-lived and vulnerable to relapse. Improving these therapies requires a deeper understanding
of human fear-related neural circuits and the ability to directly modulate them to enhance extinction learning. This
project will uncover circuit-level dynamics within amygdala-prefrontal pathways during fear extinction and regula-
tion, potentially informing the development of nucleus-speciﬁc and hemisphere-targeted AMY neuromodulation
strategies for PTSD and related disorders.

title: Assessing Design Trade-Offs in an Orthosis with Enhanced Functionality and Customizability
text:
The objective of this project is to assess various options when weighing the goals of dorsiflexion assistance
and energy recycling in a Decoupled Energy Storage and Return Variable-Stiffness Orthosis (DESR-VSO).
Doing so will shed light on how the DESR-VSO can impact the mechanics of foot drop, a condition caused by a
variety of disabilities which can lead to falling, gait compensation, and injury. The rigidity of current ankle-foot
orthoses (AFOs) limits range of motion, which compromises ankle push-off power, and the DESR-VSO seeks to
combat that technological weakness.

title: Novel ultrahigh speed swept source OCT angiography methods in diabetic retinopathy
text:
This multidisciplinary program aims to develop next generation optical coherence tomography (OCT) methods
and new imaging biomarkers of retinal microvascular and relative blood flow speeds at the capillary level for
understanding and managing diabetic retinopathy (DR). The proposed studies address impactful questions
related to clinical DR management, including early disease detection, predicting risk, monitoring disease
progression and treatment response, and improving clinical trial efficiency. The long term goal is to create an
imaging based tool to guide medical intervention and accelerate drug development, which can lead to better
preservation of visual function in DR patients.

title: Identification by High Throughput Screening of Inhibitors of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis ESX-1 and ESX-5 Type VII Secretion Systems – critical virulence determinants and novel drug targets
text:
TO PUBLIC HEALTH
Tuberculosis is a major global health problem whose treatment is unusually protracted and complicated by the
emergence of multi-drug and extensively drug resistant strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative
agent, and hence new and better drugs to treat tuberculosis are urgently needed. This project seeks to identify
small molecules that block the mycobacterial ESX-1 and ESX-5 Type VII secretion systems (T7SSs), as these
systems are essential to the capacity of the bacteria to grow and cause disease and constitute novel drug
targets. We shall screen extensive libraries of chemical compounds to identify those that block the function of
the ESX-1 and/or ESX-5 T7SS and then confirm the capacity of these inhibitors to block the capacity of the
bacteria to replicate within human host cells and the capacity of ESX-5 inhibitors additionally to block growth of
the bacteria in broth culture, thereby providing proof of principle for development of a new class of antibiotics to
treat tuberculosis.

title: Seattle Quant: A Resource for the Skyline Software Ecosystem
text:
Mass spectrometry has been a fundamental technology for the analysis of proteins in health and
disease. Quantitative mass spectrometry measurements offer a promising alternative to
immunological based assays that are the standard for quantitative protein measurements in
clinical and basic research laboratories. Critical to these experiments is our software, Skyline
and the associated ecosystem of tools, which have been developed to handle the generation of
instrument methods and the subsequent quantitative analysis of the resulting data.
